FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Utensils, 
Cutlery Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Divisional 
Council. 


Insulated container is a vacuum insulated/thermal insulated storage container that greatly lengthens the time over 
which its contents remain hotter or cooler than the container’s surroundings. The gap between the two containers 
is partially evacuated of air, creating a near-vacuum or stuffed with thermal insulation which significantly reduces 
heat transfer by conduction or convection. The cover or lid is a vacuum insulated/thermal insulated cover that 
greatly lengthens the time over which its contents remain hotter or cooler than the lid’s surroundings. The gap 
between the two layers of the lid is partially evacuated of air, creating a near-vacuum or stuffed with thermal 
insulation which significantly reduces heat transfer by conduction or convection. 


In the Indian context this type of insulated containers are also called as casserole/hot-cold box, insulated lunch 
box etc. For the purpose of simplicity and uniformity in this standard terms like casserole/hot-cold box, insulated 
lunch box etc, have been used as insulated container, where ever required. 

NOTE — The cookware utensils casseroles for use on heat source are covered in IS 14756 and IS 1660. 
While preparing this standard, assistance has been taken from BS EN 12546-2 : 2000 ‘Materials and articles in 
contact with foodstuffs. Insulated containers for domestic use: Part 2 Specification for insulated bags and boxes’. 
While implementing this standard, the manufacturer shall ensure compliance with relevant statutory regulations. 


The relevant SI units and corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance: 
Pressure | Pa (Pascal) = 1 N/m? 
1 kgf/mm? = 9.806 65 MPa 
The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex C. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17569 : 2021 


Indian Standard 


INSULATED CONTAINERS FOR 
FOOD STORAGE — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard covers minimum requirements of 
insulated containers for storage and maintaining the 
temperature of hot and cold food (solid, semi solid 
or viscous liquid) for domestic purpose upto 20 litre 
nominal capacity. 


NOTE — The insulated containers can be used for transporting 
or table top. 


1.2 The insulated containers can be of the following 
types: 
a) Plastic on the outside and stainless-steel inside; 
b) Stainless steel on both sides; 
c) Plastic on both sides; 
d) Lid or bottom container can be like a, b or c above; 


e) Lid can be of glass with beading (mainly stainless 
steel with or without silicone gasket; and 


f) Hot/cold box with inserts (stainless steel utensils 
with stainless steel/plastic lid).

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Insulated Container — Container consisting 
of inner container and an outer protective case, with 
vacuum or insulant between them. 


3.2 Nominal Capacity — Declared inner usable 
volume in litres, at room temperature required to fill 
the inner container, when in upright position, to a level 
5 mm below the top edge of the inner container. 


3.3 Table Top Use —Insulated container are generally 
provided with a handle. 


3.4 Use for Transportation — Insulated Container is 
normally provided with a strap or handle. 


4 NORMINAL CAPACITY 


4.1 The nominal capacity of insulated container shall be 
upto 20 litre and shall be expressed only in complete or 
half litre units. No negative tolerances shall be allowed 


IS 17569 : 2021 


on the nominal capacity. The Capacity shall be checked 
as given in 7.3. 
NOTE — If the Capacity of a insulated container is not 
complete or half litre units, its nominal capacity shall be 
marked as the nearest lower complete or half litre units. For 
example, in the case of a insulated container having a capacity 
of 1.9 litre, the nominal capacity to be marked shall be 1.5 litre 


5 MANUFACTURE AND WORKMANSHIP 


The shape, size and nominal capacity of the inner 
container shall be as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer. The nominal capacity of the 
inner containers shall be declared by the manufacturer. 


5.1 The insulated container shall be clean, visually 
free from distortion, dents, wrinkles, wavy surface, 
colouring, burrs, scratches, pitting, deep tool marks 
and other surface defects normally associated with 
plastics/polymer and stainless steel. 


5.2 The insulated container shall be subjected to tests 
as specified in 7. 


5.3 Metal to metal welding if done, the weld shall be 
free from welding defects. The welding electrode shall 
conform to grade 308 L (07Crl8Ni9) or higher grade as 
per IS 5856. The weld shall be finished properly so that 
when a finger is passed on the joint, it shall be smooth. 


5.4 Plastic (polymer) to plastic (polymer) welding if 
done, shall be smooth finished and shall be leakage 
proof. 


6 SAMPLING 


For the purpose of conducting the tests, three samples 
of each individual capacity shall be tested. In the event 
of one of the three samples failing the requirements, an 
additional seven samples shall be tested and these shall 
all pass. 


7 REQUIREMENTS AND TESTS 


7.1 Materials 


7.1.1 Inner Containers 


The materials used to manufacture the inner containers 
shall be stainless steel of Grade 304 as per IS 5522 or 
NI, N2, N3 of IS 15997. 


7.1.2 Outer Protective Case and Accessories 


Outer protective case and accessories shall be of 
materials which shall be rigid enough to hold the inner 
container securely under conditions of use, corrosion 
resistant and protect it from damage in normal handling. 


7.1.2.1 The outer container if coated fully or partially 
externally, shall conform to the thickness test, salt 
water corrosion test, adhesion test as per IS 9730. 
The limit for lead and cadmium of the coating shall 


be as per IS 9806 (see SI No. iv and v of Table 1, 
IS 9806) when measured as per standard test method. 
The minimum thickness of the coating shall be declared 
by the manufacturer. 


7.1.2.2 In case the outer container or lid is made 
of material other than stainless steel. The polymer 
(plastic) shall be food grade and shall not contain 
Bisphenol A (BPA). The polymer (plastic) shall have a 
thickness of minimum 1.5 mm when cut and checked 
at three different places (top, side and bottom and at the 
curvature on the end of the bottom). Supplier certificate 
shall be acceptable. 


7.1.2.3 The material used for the outer container or lid 
shall be of stainless steel as per grade 304 of IS 5522 
or NI, N2, N3 of IS 15997. The Minimum finished 
Thickness of the outer container shall be as per table 
given below: 


SI Capacity Minimum Finished 
No. Thickness of the 
outer Container 
(ml) (mm) 
(1) (2) (3) 
i) Upto 1 000 ml 0.36 
ii) Above 1 000 ml and 0.45 
upto 5 000 ml 
iii) Above 5 000 ml and 0.54 
upto 20 000 ml 


7.1.2.4 In case silicone gasket is used, it shall be 
food grade silicone, refer to Annex N of IS 3565 for 
information on silicone. 


The gasket, when visually examined, shall be free from 
blisters, pinholes, cracks, embedded foreign matters 
and other defects which may impair their serviceability. 
No Joints allowed 


NOTES 
1 Silicone manufacturers certificate for food grade is 
acceptable. 


2 Only physical and chemical properties of needs to be 
complied with for silicone gasket (inclusive of Note 1). 


7.1.2.5 In case an additional lid made of glass with 
stainless steel rim is given as accessory. The rim shall 
be made of stainless steel grade 304 of IS 5522 or N1, 
N2, N3 of IS 15997 and shall be a minimum 0.3 mm 
thick. The glass shall be as per IS 2553 (Part 1) and 
shall have minimum thickness of 3.5 mm. 


7.1.2.6 In case, thermal insulating material is used 
between the container, it shall be Polyurethane Foam 
(PUF) or any other similar thermal insulation material 
(like fabric based insulation, soft insulation etc). 


NOTE — The thermal insulating material shall be food safe 
and non-hazardous. Supplier certificate shall be acceptable. 


7.1.2.7 In case an additional lid made of stainless steel 
is given as accessory, used only, when serving of food). 
The lid shall be made of stainless steel as per grade 
304 of IS 5522 or N1, N2, N3 of IS 15997 and shall be 
same as thickness of outer container (see 7.1.2.3). 


7.1.2.8 Hot/Cold Box 


The polymer (plastics) used for inner and outer, 
container and lid shall be food grade and shall not 
contain Bisphenol A (BPA), shall conform to the 
requirements of IS 9845. The Joint could be made 
by ultrasonic welding or lock/press fit. The thickness 
shall be minimum of 1.5 mm when cut and checked 
at three different places (top, side and at the curvature 
bottom/top). 


7.1.2.9 The materials of internal utensils if given along 
with the hot/cold ox shall be made of stainless steel, 
N2 of IS 15997 or 304 series according to IS 5522. The 
thickness of utensils shall be a minimum of 0.4 mm. 
The lid can be made of plastic, which shall conform to 
the requirements of IS 9845, with minimum thickness 
of 1.5 mm. The polymer (plastics) used for inner and 
outer, container and lid shall be food grade and shall 
not contain Bisphenol A (BPA). 

CAUTION — Since this container are made for storage of 

food, if NI, N2 and N3 grades as per IS 15997 is used, avoid 

metal to metal welding. 


7.3 Capacities 


Ensure the Insulated container in empty, take water in 
a calibrated jar, pour the water from the calibrated jar 
into the insulated container, to a level 5 mm below the 
edge of the inner container, the difference in reading of 
water level in the calibrated jar is the capacity. 


7.4 Heat Retention Capability 


The temperature of water heated to 95 °C and kept 
in insulated container, in accordance with the method 
prescribed in Annex A when measured at intervals of 
1, 6, 12 and 24 h respectively, shall be not less than as 
given in Table 1. 


7.4.1 For routine testing, the insulated containers shall 
be tested for 1 h and 6 h test. Type test for 12 and 24 h 
heat retention test. 


IS 17569 : 2021 


7.5 Cold Retention Capability 


The temperature of water cooled to 5 °C and kept in 
Insulated container, in accordance with the method 
prescribed in Annex B when measured after 6 hours, 
shall be not greater than as given in Table 2. 


Table 2 Cold Retention Capability 
( Clause 7.5 )

7.6 Impact Resistance 


7.6.1 Drop Impact 


Fill water in the inner container up to its full capacity 
at the normal temperature and drop it on a hard wood 
board of 30 mm or more in thickness fixed horizontally 
from the height of 400 mm in a vertical state. Lid shall 
not come off. 


In case of insulated lunch box, there shall be no leakage. 
After the drop test, there shall be no dismantling of the 
assemble parts, deterioration in shape, dents, crack, etc. 
Same sample shall be subjected to requirements of 7.4 
and 7.5 and shall pass. 


7.6.2 Pendulum Impact 


A shoulder strap if provided, shall be subjected to the 
following test. 


Fill water in the inner container up to its full capacity 
at the normal temperature, raise the inner container to 
the position of 45 degrees by making the length of the 
shoulder strap 400 mm as shown in Fig. 1 and make 
the inner container collide with a hard wood board of 
30 mm or more in thickness fixed vertically. 


Lid shall not come off. 


In case of insulated lunch box, there shall be no leakage.

Fic. 1 PENDULUM IMPACT TEST 


After the pendulum test, there shall be no dismantling 
of the assemble parts, deterioration in shape, dents, 
crack, etc. 


Same sample shall be subjected to requirements of 7.4 
and 7.5 and shall pass. 


7.7 Strength of the Handle 


A handle if provided, shall be subjected to the following 
test. 


Fill the casserole with steel balls to 2.5 times the 
capacity of inner container (consider 1 litre of water 
at ambient temperature is equivalent to 1 Kg of water). 
Using only handle(s) of the insulated container, lift the 
insulated container | 500 times to a height of 500 mm 
and lower on to a rubber sheet kept on a level surface. 


At the end of 1 500 cycles, there shall not be any 
permanent visible distortion or weakening/loosening of 
any part of the handle assembly or assemblies. 


7.8 Test for Strength of Shoulder Strap 


A shoulder strap if provided, shall be subjected to the 
following test. 


Take a random sample other than that specified in 6. 
Put small steel balls equivalent to 10 times the weight 
(volume/capacity) of water that insulated container can 
hold. Hang the filled insulated container by a suitable 
means for 5 min (see Fig. 2). Ensure that insulated 
container is hanging freely without touching any 
surface. 


Fic. 2 TEST OF STRENGTH OF SHOULDER STRAP 
(TYPICAL ARRANGEMENT) 


After/during this test, the strap shall not break. The 
area on the insulated container to which the strap is 
fastened shall not show any signs of damage or defect. 
The elongation under load shall not exceed 10 percent 
of the total length of the strap. Initial stretching due to 
unwinding of the strap shall not be taken as elongation 
for the purpose of calculation. 


NOTE — The material of the strap may be flexible and shall 
not be affected by water. 


7.9 Leakage Test 
This test is applicable for insulated box. 


Fill the container to 75 percent of its nominal capacity 
with water at 95 degree centigrade containing 
0.5 percent surfactant. Close the lid. Thoroughly dry 
the outside surface of the lid and outer protective casing 
(container). Put the insulated container upside down 
position for at least 10 min. No drops shall appear on 
the casing or on the surface on which the insulated 
container has been over turned. 


7.10 Joint Leak Test 


This test is applicable for vaccum insulated container 
made of stainless steel. 


7.10.1 The empty insulated container is closed with the 
lid then dipped fully in a water bath for 5 min. 


7.10.2 The Insulated container and lid on removal from 
the bath shall be checked for leakage. There shall be no 
leakage inside the Insulated container or in between the 
two containers. 


7.10.3 Leakage inside the insulated container can be 
check by removing the lid and there shall be no water. 


7.10.4 Leakage in between the containers shall be 
checked for after ensuring the inside container is empty. 
Shake the insulated container and lid, there shall be no 
sound of water in between the layers. 


7.11 Staining Test - (Only for Stainless Steel) 


The inner and outer surface of the Insulated Container 
shall be thoroughly washed with hot soapy water. 
Thoroughly rinse and then degrease the test specimens 
in acetone or methylated spirits, then wiped using a soft 
cloth. The Insulated container, when dipped for 16 h in 
each of the following solutions maintained at 60 + 2 °C 
temperature, shall not show any sign of staining after 
removal from the solutions at the end of above period: 


a) Ten gram of glacial acetic acid (99 percent) 
dissolved in distilled water to make 100 ml; and 

b) Five gram of pure sodium chloride dissolved in 
distilled water to make 100 ml. 


7.12 Check for PUF (Polyurethane Foam) or any 
Other Similar Thermal Insulation Material 
Separate sample other than as specified in 6 is taken and 
cut to check the insulating material. The same sample 
can be used for checking of container thickness. 


7.13 Dimensions and Designs 


7.13.1 Length of the Shoulder Strap 


The length of the shoulder strap, if provided, shall be 
400 mm or over when measured as given in Fig. 3 and 
the length of strap shall be adjustable. 


7.13.2 Stability of Insulated Container 


When the Insulated container filled with water to 
the full capacity is placed upright over a rough 
10° inclined plane, it shall not overturn or fall or shall 
not overbalance. 


7.13.3 Cleaning 


The inner container of the insulated container shall be 
designed is such a way that it shall be possible to clean 
it easily and completely. 


NOTE — After all tests are performed, the sample Insulated 
container which was tested shall pass the Leakage test. 


IS 17569 : 2021 


Fic. 3 TyPICAL ARRANGEMENT FOR TESTING 
LENGTH OF THE STRAP 


7.14 Seepage Test 


Fill the internal container up to 25 percent with blue 
coloured water (water with blue indelible ink). Close 
the insulated container and shake the container up and 
down through a distance of 200 (+ 50) mm, 25 times in 
15 (+2) s. 

Empty the container, dry wipe all the exposed surfaces 
of container and lid. 

Dismantle or cut apart the container and lid to assess 


any seepage into the insulation material. There shall be 
no seepage. 


8 INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE 


8.1 Insulated container shall carry adequate instructions 
to the user for its proper use to ensure satisfactory 
performance. 


8.2 The Manufacturer shall provide the following 
minimum information along with each insulated 
container given below: 

a) How to unpack and take care of environment; 

b) How to stock the Insulated Container in case the 
Insulated Container is not going to be used, to 
avoid pitting or getting contaminated; 

c) Wash thoroughly before and after use; 


IS 17569 : 2021 


d) Always rinse with clean water (preferably warm 
water) before each use; 


e) Ensure the Insulated Container is cleaned, empty 
and dry before stocking after each use; 


f) Do not use for carrying ice cubes; 
g) Do not use to store or carry carbonated drinks; 


h) In order to minimize bacterial growth, do not use 
to keep warm milk products or baby food for long. 
follow b, c and ensure dry before using warm milk 
or baby food. the Insulated container should not 
stink and should be properly sterilized first with 
hot water and later rinsed with or/purified drinking 
water. ensure the Insulated container is dry and 
does not stink; 


j) The container should be periodically cleaned; 


k) Do not use in microwave oven, unless specified 
by the manufacturer by indicating on the insulated 
container; 


m) Never use in a dishwasher, unless otherwise stated 
by the manufacturer; 


n) Never use the stainless-steel insulated container 
or lid if there is suspected leakage between the 
two containers. (empty the insulated container or 
lid in dipped in water completely and shake the 
insulated container and lid after taking out from 
the water, there should be no sound of water in 
between the inner and outer containers); 


p) When disposing off plastic and PUF, please ensure 
it is done as per government guidelines. 


q) Handle the insulated container properly, do not 
drop; and 


r) Keep these instructions safely. 
9 MARKING 


9.1 Each insulated container shall be legibly and 
permanently marked with the following minimum 
information: 

a) Declared nominal capacity; 

b) Grade of material of inner container and outer 

container along with applicable IS No; 

c) Name or trade mark of the manufacturer; 

d) Batch number; 

f) Type of insulation used; and 


e) Declaration if, microwave oven safe or not to use 
in microwave oven. 


9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10 PACKAGING 


Each Insulated container shall be suitable packaged to 
avoid any damage during transit. The packaging shall 
be eco-friendly. 


IS 17569 : 2021 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 7.4 ) 
TEST FOR HEAT RETENTION CAPACITY 


A-1 GENERAL 


A-1.1 The heat retention capacity of an insulated 
container is determined by filling hot water at 95 °C in 
it in the manner prescribed in A-2 and measuring the 
temperature of water at intervals of 1, 6, 12 and 24 h, 
respectively. While carrying out the test, maintain the 
atmospheric conditions at 27+2 °C and 65+5 percent 
RH. The samples are to be pre-conditioned at 95+2 °C 
for a minimum period of two hours before starting the 
test. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 Rinse the inner container with water at 
95 + 2 °C , drain out water. Quickly fill with boiling 
water. Allow the temperature to drop slowly to 95 °C, 
close the insulated container with lid and note the time. 
Note the temperature of water in the inner container at 
the end of 1, 6, 12 or 24 h respectively from the time the 
water in the inner container attained the temperature of 
95 *C. 

NOTES — In no case shall the inner container be disturbed or 

opened except for measuring the temperature as stated above. 


A-2.2 The insulated container shall be taken as having 
passed the test, if the temperatures measured at the end 
of 1, 6, 12 and 24 h are not less than those specified 
in 7.4. 


ANNEX B 
( Clause 7.5 ) 
TEST FOR COLD RETENTION CAPACITY 


B-1 GENERAL 


B-1.1 The cold retention capacity of an inner container 
is determined by filling cold water at 5 °C in it in 
the manner prescribed below and measuring the 
temperature of water after 6 hours. The samples shall 
be pre-conditioned at 5 + 1 °C for a minimum period of 
two hours before starting the test. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Rinse the inner container with water at 5 + 1 °C, 
drain out water. Quickly fill container up to the neck 


with ice cold water. Allow the temperature to increase 
slowly to 5 °C, close the container with the lid and note 
the time. Note the temperature of water in the inner 
container at the end of six hours. 


NOTES — In no case shall the inner container be disturbed or 
opened except for measuring the temperature as stated above. 


B-2.2 The insulated container shall be taken as having 
passed the test if the temperature measured at the end of 
6 h shall not be greater than that specified in 7.5 


IS 17569 : 2021

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 33 (15558).
